tasks.title: Merge settings
tasks.statement: Write a function merge(defaults, custom) that returns a new dictionary containing all the pairs of both dictionaries; when keys match, custom wins. The original dictionaries must not be changed.
tasks.hint: defaults | custom: the right dictionary overrides the left; or copy + update.

tasks.title: A dict from two lists
tasks.statement: Write a function to_dict(keys, values) that returns a dictionary where the i-th key is paired with the i-th value. The lists have the same length. Use dict and zip.

tasks.title: Invert a dict
tasks.statement: Write a function invert(d) that returns a dictionary with keys and values swapped. The values of the original dictionary are unique strings. Do it in a single expression with a dictionary comprehension.
tasks.hint: {value: key for key, value in d.items()}.

tasks.title: Words by first letter
tasks.statement: Write a function group_by_first(words) that returns a dictionary where each key is the first letter of a word and each value is the list of words starting with that letter, in the original order. The words are non-empty.

tasks.title: The most frequent word
tasks.statement: Write a function most_common(words) that returns the most frequent word of a non-empty list. If several words tie, return the one that appeared earlier in the list. Count the frequencies and find the maximum by value.
tasks.hint: max(counts, key=counts.get) returns the key with the largest value, and on a tie, the first one.

tasks.title: Names of adults
tasks.statement: Write a function adult_names(users), where users is a list of dictionaries {'name': ..., 'age': ...}. Return the list of names of those who are 18 or older, in the original order.
tasks.hint: [u['name'] for u in users if u['age'] >= 18].

tasks.title: Sort by age
tasks.statement: Write a function sort_by_age(users) that returns a list of the same records {'name': ..., 'age': ...}, sorted by age from youngest to oldest. Define a small helper function to use as the sort key.
tasks.hint: def get_age(user): return user['age'], and then sorted(users, key=get_age).

tasks.title: Grade as a word
tasks.statement: Write a function grade_word(grade): 5 -> «excellent», 4 -> «good», 3 -> «satisfactory», 2 -> «bad», anything else -> «unknown». No if chain: use a lookup table in a dictionary.
tasks.hint: `return words.get(grade, 'unknown')`, where the dictionary words holds pairs like `5: 'excellent'` and so on.
